Subject: Annual token engagement scaling and overview (starter/growth/enterprise)

Hi Sana —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our conversation about annual commits for VeloxAI, attached is a first-pass proposal that lays out three commitment bands (Starter, Growth, Enterprise), breakpoint pricing per 1k tokens, and a few operational guardrails we recommend to avoid bill shock. High level:

- Starter (onramp): 0.5M tokens/mo avg, 12-month term, nominal discount from list
- Growth (scale): 5M tokens/mo avg, 12-month term, meaningful breakpoint discounts and smoothing credits
- Enterprise (predictable): 25M+ tokens/mo, optional dedicated capacity and SLA, largest effective discounts + carryover allowance

Two non-obvious pieces I highlighted in the sheet:
1) Carryover + smoothing: we allow a limited token carryover (up to 15% of committed monthly average) for the Growth and Enterprise tiers and a 60-day smoothing window to spread short-term spikes.
2) Overage guardrail: when you exceed the smoothing window we apply a capped overage rate (not list) and provide a one-time advance credit for the first large spike in year 1 to reduce risk while you optimize prefix caching.

I've attached: velox_annual_commit_matrix_v1.xlsx (matrix + worked examples), a short one-pager on the overage guardrails, and a sample MPA for legal.

Two asks from your side to help us finalize:
- Confirm which tier you think maps to expected 12–18 month volume ramp (Starter vs Growth).
- If procurement/legal wants a first read, please share the contact and we can produce a redline-friendly MPA (DocuSign-ready).

Happy to jump back on a quick 30-min call if you want to walk through the matrix row-by-row.

Thanks,

Sana — quick answers below and a suggested path forward.

1) Smoothing window mechanics: the 60-day window is retrospective and used to smooth billing when spikes occur. Practically: month N's usage is compared to the trailing 60-day average and any excess within the 60-day window is eligible for smoothing credit up to the carryover cap. We do this to avoid forward-crediting token allowances.

2) Growth ramp profile (recommended conservative baseline):
- Month 1: 20% of committed monthly average
- Month 2: 35%
- Month 3: 55%
- Month 4: 75%
- Month 5: 90%
- Month 6+: 100%

We included a variant in tab 3 of the spreadsheet that shows an accelerated ramp for customers expecting immediate production load. If you expect a faster rollout (Q3 feature toggle schedule), we can shift the breakpoint sooner and increase the initial credits accordingly.

Procurement/legal: happy to send a redline-friendly MPA. Marissa (cc'd) will own the commercial language and Neha will coordinate billing/finance items (carryover accounting and reporting).

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm tier selection (Starter vs Growth) by EOW 6/26.
- We schedule a 30-min walkthrough with Alvaro and your procurement on 6/28 or 6/29 — I can hold time.
- We'll then generate an MPA draft with the agreed ramp and carryover terms and route for legal review.

Attaching the MPA sample again: redwood_mpa_sample.pdf

Rishi

Quick note from my side — for Growth -> Enterprise conversion we usually offer a one-time conversion credit that preserves smoothing history and avoids double-billing during the transition month. If VeloxAI is likely to hit committed volume earlier than projected, call this out during the walkthrough and we can bake the conversion step into the MPA with explicit dates.

Also: Enterprise customers frequently take optional dedicated capacity for predictable latency; we can price that as an add-on line item with its own SLA. Happy to cover add-on pricing on the call.
